title: A turn's end is written only to the caller's output, so nothing on the agent's own machine says how its last turn ended
foundBy: session agent, maintainer of this repository and of a harness that drives these tools, while designing how that harness should read a failure class

evidence.verified: `go test ./internal/cli/ -count=1` passes with the new `turn_log_test.go`. The provider failure tests for all three drivers fail against the old drivers with `ended a turn and left no line`. In real sandboxes, a codex turn refused with an injected rate limit left `5 throttled 12.5 turn failed: rate limit exceeded` in `~/.cs-turns/codex.log`. An opencode turn left `5 throttled 7`, and a successful turn left `0 - - -`. A fleet harness read those lines through its probe and waited the throttle out. Claude was checked by unit test only, because the host's login had expired.

notes.text: The log is written by an EXIT trap in each driver, so every exit path is covered by one piece of code. `--state`, `--help` and a usage error write nothing. A driver that is killed writes nothing, so a missing line means the ending is not known. The file keeps between 200 and 400 lines, and `CS_TURN_LOG` names another path.
